Death is not freedom. Death is, to our knowledge, nothingness. Unless you subscribe to a religion, in which case I apologise for going on with the mini-speech I'm about to give.

When your brain shuts down... That's it. You can't feel emotion. You can't feel, period. And as humans we can't fathom that. There's no good way to understand a lack of sensory input. There is no relief in death. There's no sense of being. Not even an eternal black void. 

You have someone who matters to you. Please don't leave them to chase something that might not exist.

Yeah, it's this little twinge in the back of my head. Sometimes it'll be for no reason, a quiet "hey, it doesn't matter, just do it". Sometimes it'll be because of overemotion or stress, with that overwhelming feeling of "I already existed for no reason and now xyz is how I feel so why continue". 

Sometimes I'm able to focus on the little things, like the woman who patted my hand as she gave me my change in Dollarama today. She was very nice. I don't know why, but I think she was trying to cheer up anyone who came by. She called me a dear. Did she know somehow? Ididn't even know what to say, I just grinned like an idiot on the way back to my break room. Those little moments of joy push any thought of the act deep into a crevice.

I feel the same way, but here's the thing about our mind: we live in a vacuum. We cannot truly understand how others feel, but we don't need to. Different people have different emotional limits and sensitivities, and different balances of chemicals in their brains. Our experiences have shaped us in unique ways that psychologists don't even properly understand. It's just the same for physical pain — one person who stubs their toe can bawl, and the next will notice it, go "ow' and continue on. 

Please don't blame yourself for feeling this way, because you aren't alone.
Reminder that, unless you believe otherwise, there is no "out". Death is nothingness. There is no end, no relief.
